fuzz: queries racing with committed writes never mix revisions and never return an unreadable row
filters: comparison semantics, null vs missing, in/contains/exists/isNull, boolean nesting
unknown fields fail early with a structured error
null/missing semantics through records
sort: explicit null policy, stable ties, descending, multi-key
head/tail/limit/offset edge cases and sort+tail equivalence
uniq removes adjacent duplicates, distinct removes global duplicates
aggregates: count(*) vs count(field), typing, empty input, coercion
select/pluck/rename and type errors
lines: cat/readLines/range, CRLF, no trailing newline, Unicode, byte ranges, empty documents
cut: code points by default, bytes explicitly, ranges clipped and merged, fields
grep/regex/replace/trim/split/sed subset
regex safety: nested quantifiers, backreferences and lookaround are rejected before any work
time operators: after is inclusive, before exclusive, between half-open (or closed on request), recent/latest tie-break
join: inner/left/semi/anti, null keys never match, duplicate keys multiply, lookup takes the first match
set operations: union, unionAll, intersect, except with duplicates
subqueries: `in` with a nested query is evaluated once with the same snapshot
graph: references, backlinks, related, traverse (cycles, depth, node caps, edge types)
the engine never trusts the source: unordered supersets that ignore filters give the same answers
scope: workspace + shared defaults, collection narrowing, includeShared:false
budgets: row cap with cursor, byte cap, buffer cap on blocking operators, deadline, cancellation
early termination: head stops reading documents
saved queries: resolved through the source, refinements compose, cycles are rejected
explain: stages, pushdown and warnings without reading documents
derived text prefilter: contains body becomes a search request, and results are still exact
validator: unknown keys (including a forged principal), depth, size and strictness
capabilities: semantic and hybrid are declared unavailable with a reason
forged principal in the execution context is refused
every operator family returns the same rows through SDK, CLI and MCP
ACL parity: MCP under a restricted host identity equals the SDK under the same identity
MCP: structured errors, forged principal and unknown keys are rejected, tightening-only budgets, explain and capabilities
CLI: stream aliases compose through pipes and match the AST; formats; explain; saved queries; exit codes
cursor paging through CLI: stderr carries the cursor, a second call continues
kill at journal.before_append: after recovery every acknowledged commit is queryable, nothing partial is, and cat/search agree
kill at revision.after_dirsync: after recovery every acknowledged commit is queryable, nothing partial is, and cat/search agree
kill at journal.after_append_before_fsync: after recovery every acknowledged commit is queryable, nothing partial is, and cat/search agree
kill at journal.after_fsync: after recovery every acknowledged commit is queryable, nothing partial is, and cat/search agree
kill at head.before_replace: after recovery every acknowledged commit is queryable, nothing partial is, and cat/search agree
kill at view.before_replace: after recovery every acknowledged commit is queryable, nothing partial is, and cat/search agree
killing a process mid-query leaves the vault untouched and the next query correct
derived state damage: deleted, truncated or foreign manifest and SQLite files give correct answers, never silently incomplete ones
writer processes racing with a querying process: no query ever misses an acknowledged commit that preceded it
ranking and scores of readable rows do not depend on hidden documents; hidden titles never appear in errors
paths: traversal strings and absolute paths are plain values, never file reads
symlink swap: a revision file replaced by a link to outside content is never served
malicious YAML in a stored revision cannot crash the engine or leak; other rows still answer
resource abuse: huge lines, oversized sorts, wide joins and deep graphs stay inside budgets
saved queries cannot carry a principal, code, or unsafe regex; a saved query cannot widen scope beyond the reader
cursor tampering: edited, replayed on another query, or forged cursors are refused
the query layer holds no write path: the AST has no operator that writes, and the journal is untouched by a hostile battery
sources, scope defaults, collection narrowing and metadata projections come from the manifest (no document is read)
search modes: exact, keyword, regex and auto go through the index-backed engine, with transparent backend info
semantic and hybrid: CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE unless a labelled downgrade is explicitly requested; lexical results are never mislabelled
hydration is pinned to the snapshot revision and counted
search sees commits after the snapshot consistently: edited, created and deleted objects
filesystem and SQLite give the same rows for the same queries (and the files path works with SQLite disabled)
ACL: an agent sees only its workspace and wiki; a stranger sees nothing; no counts, scores, snippets or edges leak
ACL changes take effect on the next query (grant and revoke), cursors are bound to the principal and query
forged identity: the principal cannot be supplied in a query or context
graph over a real vault: references resolve titles, traversal respects readability at every hop
observations: recent/timeline/session/between agree with the memory recall API
saved queries are versioned objects: saved through Vault, readable under ACL, refinable
read-only: running queries never writes to the journal or canonical objects
indexed queries do not materialize the corpus: documents read is proportional to the answer

gaps.reason: See verification/query/benchmarks/: 1K and 10K are measured; a 100K corpus takes over an hour to build through the fsynced commit protocol. Recorded as NOT_RUN unless verification/query/benchmarks/100k.json exists.
No embedding provider exists. Capability negotiation is tested (CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE, labelled keyword downgrade only on request); real semantic retrieval is not implemented.

gaps.item: SQL pushdown of metadata, time and graph operators
gaps.reason: SQLite accelerates text search only (FTS5/trigram via the existing engine). Metadata, time and graph operators run on the journal-synced manifest, which is in memory and file-only; they are not SQL.
Blocking operators are bounded by maxBufferRows and fail with RESOURCE_LIMIT rather than spilling.
JavaScript RegExp with conservative pattern rules and an 8 KiB per-line window; documented in docs/query.md.
All results were produced on macOS/APFS.
A cursor is bound to the journal sequence; after any commit it fails with SNAPSHOT_EXPIRED unless allowCursorDrift is requested (then results may shift).

gaps.item: Integration with the final retrieval-optimizer branch
gaps.reason: Developed in an isolated copy (Engram-query) against the retrieval code as it stood at copy time. Merge into the main tree and re-running verify:all is pending.

limitations: Search-backed queries pin every returned row to the snapshot revision and re-verify objects that changed after the snapshot, but the text index itself is read at its own checkpoint.
Semantics of default ordering: id ascending for non-search queries, relevance for search; any other order must be requested.
